analysis.investment_thesis: Greaves Cotton is a legacy industrial-to-EV transition story that has destroyed shareholder value over the last decade, with negative net profits in 3 of last 5 years, ROE of just 4.1%, and FCF negative for 4 consecutive years. Until the EV segment (Ampere/ELE) demonstrates real profitability — not just revenue — there is no margin of safety at 34.6x P/E on near-zero earnings.
key_strengths: Low leverage (D/E 0.12) provides balance sheet cushion during transition
Revenue recovering to ₹2,918 Cr in FY25, up from ₹1,500 Cr trough in FY21
India EV 3-wheeler segment is a structural tailwind with government policy support
key_risks: Catastrophic profitability collapse — operating margins from 12.5% (FY16) to 3.94% (FY25), ROE at 4.1% vs my 15% minimum threshold
Free cash flow negative in 4 of last 5 years; OCF positive in only 1 of last 5 years — the business is a cash incinerator right now
EV segment has not yet proven unit economics; FY24 saw a ₹367 Cr net loss (likely write-downs), signalling prior capital misallocation
red_flags: Net losses in FY21, FY22, and FY24 — chronic inability to convert revenue to profit
Finance costs rising at 36.1% CAGR while operating profits shrink — leverage creep
Other income of -₹270 Cr in FY24 signals large impairments or investment losses, obscuring true operating weakness
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Greaves Cotton is a textbook case of a legacy industrial business caught in an expensive technology transition it has yet to execute profitably. The company pivoted from diesel engines toward EVs (Ampere 2-wheelers, ELE e-rickshaws) — a directionally right bet on India's EV adoption — but the financials tell a painful story. Operating profit CAGR is -4.3% over 9 years. Net profits have been negative in FY21, FY22, and FY24, and FY25 is barely breakeven at -₹6 Cr. ROCE at 5.13% means the company is not even earning its cost of capital — I would never buy a business that destroys value on every rupee deployed. The gross margin of 32.7% shows the core product economics are not the problem; it's operating leverage and transition costs that are eating everything.

From my perspective, valuation makes this even more difficult to hold. At 34.6x trailing P/E on near-zero earnings, the market is pricing in a sharp recovery that the company has failed to deliver for years. The forward P/E of 18.55x implies analysts expect a significant earnings turnaround — possible, but I want to see it, not pay for it in advance. Promoter holding at 55.8% is stable, which is the only governance comfort here. Greaves has been around since 1859 and will survive, but survival is not a thesis for buying at these levels. I would watch this from the sidelines — if operating margins cross 7-8% sustainably and FCF turns positive for two consecutive years, it deserves a fresh look.
